slides.headline: He built India's first digital computer. Decades later, he built the machine that counts India's votes.
Dr. A. S. Rao was born on September 20, 1914
slides.body: Rao founded the Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL) in 1967, tasked with building India's electronics and computing capability from near zero, at a time when computers were imported, foreign-built machines.

slides.headline: ECIL's TDC series became India's first indigenously designed digital computers.
slides.body: Under Rao, ECIL didn't just assemble foreign designs - it designed and manufactured computers domestically through the 1970s, giving India its own computing base at a time almost no developing country had one.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: The same institution later built the EVM and VVPAT machines used in Indian elections today.
slides.body: A company founded to prove India could build its own computers went on to build the machines that record and verify how a billion-plus people vote - a direct line from one founder's mandate to the mechanics of the world's largest democracy.
